text.p: Dutch planemaker Fokker NV Thursday appeared on the point of losing its protracted battle to stay in the air, signalling despair for one of the oldest marques in aviation history. The following is a chronology of the main events in the company's history.
* 1912 -- Anthony Fokker begins building planes for German army, including fighters like the Fokker triplane favoured by the Red Baron in World War One.
* 1919 -- Fokker established as a commercial company.
* 1928 -- Fokker is world's biggest planemaker, designing revolutionary aircraft like the Fokker IV which made aviation history with a coast-to-coast crossing of the United States in 1922.
* 1957 -- Fokker launches the famous F27 Fokker Friendship turboprop, still in service 30 years later.
* 1969 -- Fokker enters cooperation pact with German aerospace manufacturer VFW, but the relationship is tense from the start.
* 1980 -- Fokker and VFW go their separate ways.
* 1981 -- Fokker and McDonnell Douglas of the United States decide to work together.
* 1983 -- Fokker launches plans to build the F50 and F100 jets at a development cost of 1.6 billion guilders ($930.2 million).
* 1985/86 -- F50 and F100 make their debut flights.
* 1986 -- Fokker shares hit a high of 99.50 guilders ($57.85) on optimism about F50 and F100 programmes.
* 1987 -- Dutch state saves Fokker from threat of bankruptcy caused by spiraling development costs, taking 49 percent equity stake in company.
* 1990 -- Fokker recovers, posts profit of Dfl 83 million ($48.3 million).
* 1991 -- Fokker sets out to find new industry partner.
* 1993 -- Daimler-Benz AG's DASA unit agrees to pay 686 million guilders for a 51 percent stake in Fokker.
* 1994 -- Fokker announces first of a string of heavy losses and sacks 1,100 of its 13,000 workforce.
* JULY 1994 -- Dutch government and DASA pump an additional one billion guilders ($581.4 million) of fresh capital into the company.
* AUGUST 1995 -- Fokker posts record first-half loss of 651 million guilders ($378.5 million). Shares slump to 5.60 guilders ($3.26).
* SEPTEMBER 1995 -- Two major shareholders, DASA and Dutch state, refuse Fokker request for another 2.3 billion guilders ($1.3 billion).
* JANUARY 1996
-- Daimler Benz cuts off financial support. Dutch state says will explore other rescue options.
-- Canada's Bombardier surfaces as possible saviour.
-- Dutch state offers 255 million guilder ($148.3 million) credit line to keep Fokker alive while it looks for buyer.
* FEBRUARY 1996
-- Fokker says it is in talks with five serious potential buyers (Samsung, British Aerospace, Italy's Aerospatiale, Taiwanese government and Bombardier)
-- Bombardier says no longer interested.
* MARCH 1996 -- Fokker declares bankruptcy at three core units. Non-core businesses such as space systems, electronics and aircraft services live on, but need new partners.
* APRIL 1996 -- Fokker says Samsung no longer interested in bidding for company.
* JUNE 1996 -- Fokker remains in production after Dutch airline KLM orders seven 70-seat aircraft.
* JULY 1996 -- Dutch industrial systems group Stork buys Fokker Aviation, Fokker's parts, maintenance and special services unit.
* AUGUST 1996 -- Samsung re-emerges as possible buyer.
* SEPTEMBER 1996 -- Samsung begins due diligence procedures.
* OCTOBER 1996 -- Samsung hands Fokker business plan to Dutch Economics Ministry.
-- Samsung, Economics Ministry delegates begin talks on Fokker re-launch.
-- Administrators tell staff that rescue deadline is end-October.
* NOVEMBER 5, 1996 -- Dutch government expects decision on Samsung takeover "within days."
* NOVEMBER 13, 1996 -- Samsung invites Korea's Daewoo and Hyundai to take part in Fokker rescue.
* NOVEMBER 28, 1996 -- Court-appointed administrators at Fokker ended rescue talks with Samsung after Shorts, one of Fokker's suppliers, said it would no longer supply wings for Fokker jets.
-- Dutch government and administrators hold out little hope of new bidder emerging, suggesting that final Fokker plane will roll out in May followed by liquidation.
